facts.statement: The CLI is located at scripts/tasks.py relative to the skill directory.
Look for a .tasks.yaml config by walking up from the working directory; when none exists, run init in the project root, which creates the config and the artifacts directory that holds task files.
Resolve the author once from, in order: the new --author flag, the config author field, git config user.name, then $USER — the CLI picks the first that works.

Change state, updated, created, or parent only through the CLI (new, set, set-state) so updated stays correct; edit the body (descriptions, checklists, ## Links lines, ## Open Questions) with normal file tools — the Gotchas restate it: the body is the only part you edit by hand.
States are draft, open, in-progress, complete, plus invalid.
The chain draft → open → in-progress → complete is descriptive only: any state may transition to any other via set-state.
Mark a task invalid when it will never be done (superseded, wrong premise, duplicate), and always pass --reason with a free-text explanation; it is recorded in the reason frontmatter field.
Create a subtask with new subtask --parent <id>; the parent must exist and be a task or bug — subtasks cannot have subtasks.
Scan the project before writing: read the relevant code and docs, check git log, and run list and grep over existing tasks; never ask the user a question the repository can answer.

Verify the request's claims against the code — confirm referenced files, functions, and endpoints exist, and reproduce the bug when possible; put anything unverifiable in ## Open Questions and leave the task in draft until it is resolved.
Answer why, how, and definition-of-done — the template's ## Why, ## How, and ## Definition of Done sections.
Write the definition of done as a checkable bullet list.

A title containing "and" means two chunks of work: file two tickets (or a parent task with subtasks), even when asked for a single ticket; the same applies when the definition of done needs more than three bullets — one ticket is one chunk of work.
Write the title as the symptom, not the suspected cause.
Number the minimal reproduction steps and start each from a known state.
Keep expected behavior and actual behavior as separate sections.
Quote error messages verbatim, including the full traceback when there is one.
Record the environment where the bug reproduced.
File one bug per ticket.

Record relationships in the ## Links section with exactly four tokens — RELATED TO:, DEPENDS ON:, DUPLICATES:, INVALIDATES: — each followed by comma- or space-separated task filenames; tokens must be uppercase with the colon, otherwise links and validate cannot see them.
Grep the corpus for existing duplicates and related work before creating a new task or bug.
Link semantics are informational — DEPENDS ON does not block completion.
Task numbers come from a global per-project sequence and are never reused; a deleted task leaves a permanent gap.
Run validate after bulk edits (renames, scripted changes, manual frontmatter fixes) to catch dangling link targets and stray files.

Use set <id> updated <date> only to repair a stale timestamp; every CLI write refreshes updated automatically, so a backdated updated signals a manual repair; backdating to make a task look touched for a report is not a repair — decline and offer the real updated instead.

excluded.reason: show/list/grep routing is baseline CLI discovery; the CLI's own -h is the documented source and a fresh agent finds subcommands without the skill
excluded.statement: Use show to read a task, list with filters to survey the corpus, and grep to search bodies with ripgrep syntax.
